baslik: The Great Lakes Freighter That Vanished Without a Mayday
sonuc: sank in a Lake Superior storm without a distress call
tetik: heavy seas flooding the hull in a violent storm
mekanizma: progressive flooding, attributed by the Coast Guard to leaking hatch covers; other theories cite shoal damage
ders: Great Lakes load-line and safety rules were revised
zincir: SHIP REPORTS DAMAGE AND A LIST
yanilgi: Nobody knows the cause for certain. Investigators disagreed: leaking hatches, a shoal strike, or giant waves.
tartisma: Investigators reached different conclusions from the same wreck. How do you decide when evidence is incomplete?
basliklar: Why the Edmund Fitzgerald Sank
The Freighter Lost Without a Mayday
sahneler: In a November storm, a giant freighter vanished on Lake Superior.
It sank without a distress call, and all twenty nine crew were killed.
The captain had reported damage and a list.
Water was getting into the hull.
The Coast Guard blamed leaking hatch covers.
Others argued it struck a shoal or was hit by huge waves.
The wreck lies broken in two on the lake floor.
Great Lakes safety rules were revised afterward.

baslik: The Overloaded Ferry That Told Passengers to Stay Put
sonuc: capsized off South Korea's southwest coast
tetik: a sharp turn on an overloaded, top-heavy ferry
mekanizma: loss of stability from modifications, excess cargo and reduced ballast water
ders: South Korea overhauled ferry inspections and coast guard response
yanilgi: The turn alone wasn't enough to sink a sound ship. Modifications and overloading had already stripped away its stability.
tartisma: Passengers were told to stay in their cabins. When does following instructions become dangerous?
basliklar: Why the Sewol Ferry Capsized
The Ferry Made Top-Heavy Before It Sailed
sahneler: A South Korean ferry rolled over and sank on a routine trip.
Most passengers were trapped, and three hundred four people died.
Many were high school students.
Extra cabins had been added to the top of the ship.
It carried far more cargo than allowed, with less ballast below.
A sharp turn tipped it past recovery.
Passengers were told to stay in their cabins.
Ferry inspections and rescue response were overhauled afterward.

baslik: The Tanker That Ran Onto a Reef It Knew Was There
sonuc: ran aground and spilled oil into Prince William Sound
tetik: a missed turn around a charted reef
mekanizma: grounding on Bligh Reef after a planned turn was not executed, with a single hull
ders: the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 phased in double-hulled tankers
yanilgi: The reef was well known and charted. The tanker hit it because a planned turn was never made.
tartisma: The crew was short-staffed and tired. How much of the blame belongs to staffing decisions?
basliklar: Why the Exxon Valdez Ran Aground
The Missed Turn That Spilled Millions of Gallons
sahneler: A supertanker ran onto a reef in Alaska's Prince William Sound.
Its hull ripped open and crude oil spread across the water.
The reef was well known and on every chart.
The tanker had left the shipping lane to avoid ice.
It needed to turn back, and the turn wasn't made.
The crew was short-staffed and tired.
A single hull was all that held the oil in.
US law then phased in double-hulled tankers.

baslik: A Supertanker's Steering Failed — Then Came the Towing Argument
sonuc: ran aground off Brittany and broke apart
tetik: a failure of its hydraulic steering gear in a storm
mekanizma: steering gear failure followed by delayed towing and grounding
ders: steering redundancy and emergency towing rules for tankers were strengthened
yanilgi: The tanker didn't sink right away. It drifted for hours while help was negotiated.
tartisma: Towing terms were debated while the ship drifted. Should rescue ever wait for a contract?
basliklar: Why the Amoco Cadiz Ran Aground
The Supertanker That Lost Its Steering
sahneler: A supertanker drifted onto the rocks off Brittany and broke apart.
Within days, its entire cargo of crude oil had spilled.
Its hydraulic steering had failed in a storm.
The ship drifted toward the shore.
A tug arrived, but towing terms were discussed first.
When a line was finally attached, it broke.
Hours later, the tanker grounded.
Rules on tanker steering and emergency towing were strengthened.

baslik: Why Wartime Liberty Ships Cracked in Half
sonuc: cracked and some broke in two
tetik: welded steel turning brittle in cold seas
mekanizma: brittle fracture in welded hulls, starting at sharp corners and weld defects
ders: Constance Tipper's research made steel toughness a design requirement
yanilgi: Welding wasn't the mistake on its own. The steel became brittle in the cold, and a welded hull gave a crack nothing to stop at.
tartisma: Mass production won the war at sea. Were the losses an acceptable price for speed?
basliklar: Why Liberty Ships Broke in Half
The Cold Steel That Cracked Wartime Ships
sahneler: During the Second World War, some cargo ships suddenly cracked apart.
A few suddenly split completely in two, even at the dock.
They were Liberty ships, built fast by welding.
In cold water, their steel turned brittle.
Cracks started at sharp corners and weld defects.
A welded hull is one piece, so a crack had nothing to stop it.
Metallurgist Constance Tipper showed how the steel failed.
Steel toughness then became a basic design requirement.

baslik: How One Ship Blocked the Suez Canal for Six Days
sonuc: wedged itself across the Suez Canal
tetik: strong winds acting on a stack of containers
mekanizma: wind loading on a very tall container stack plus hydrodynamic bank effect in a narrow channel
ders: the canal widened and deepened its southern section
zincir: TALL STACK ACTS LIKE A SAIL
yanilgi: No engine failure stopped it. Wind and the pull of the canal's banks swung the ship sideways.
tartisma: Ships keep growing while the canal stays narrow. Who should pay for infrastructure to keep up?
basliklar: Why the Ever Given Blocked the Suez Canal
The Wind and the Bank Effect
sahneler: A giant container ship wedged itself sideways across the Suez Canal.
Within hours, global shipping was blocked for six days.
Strong winds were blowing during a sandstorm.
Its tall stack of containers caught the wind like a sail.
In a narrow canal, water flow near the bank pulls a ship's stern.
Engineers call this the bank effect.
The bow drove into one bank and the stern into the other.
The canal later widened its southern section.

baslik: The Thames Pleasure Boat That Sank Into Sewage
sonuc: was cut in two on the Thames
tetik: a collision with a much larger collier
mekanizma: collision in a busy river with unclear navigation rules, then drowning in polluted water
ders: Thames navigation rules and the treatment of London's sewage were reformed
yanilgi: Many victims didn't drown from the collision itself. They struggled in water full of raw sewage released minutes before.
tartisma: London's sewage outfall had just opened nearby. Should the city share the blame?
basliklar: Why the Princess Alice Sank
The Collision in London's Sewage
sahneler: A crowded pleasure steamer was cut in two on the River Thames.
Within minutes, it sank and hundreds of people drowned.
A much larger collier had struck it.
The two ships misread each other's passing move.
Raw sewage had just been released into the river nearby.
Survivors struggled in foul water.
It became one of Britain's worst inland disasters.
River rules and London's sewage treatment were reformed.

baslik: One Control Rod Pulled Too Far Destroyed a Reactor
sonuc: exploded during maintenance
tetik: a single control rod pulled out too far by hand
mekanizma: prompt criticality from manual withdrawal of the central control rod, causing a steam explosion
ders: reactors were designed so no single rod can make them critical
yanilgi: The reactor wasn't running. It was restarted by hand, one rod at a time, and that single rod was enough.
tartisma: One rod could make the reactor critical by itself. Should any single action ever be able to cause disaster?
basliklar: Why the SL-1 Reactor Exploded
The Single Control Rod That Went Too Far
sahneler: A small military reactor in Idaho exploded during maintenance.
In an instant, all three men working on it were killed.
They were reconnecting its central control rod.
That rod had to be lifted by hand.
It was pulled far too high.
The reactor went critical and flashed water to steam.
The blast lifted the reactor vessel off its mounts.
Reactors were then designed so no single rod can do this.

baslik: The Reactor Fire Saved by a Filter Called a Folly
sonuc: caught fire and released radioactive material
tetik: a heating procedure to release stored energy in the graphite
mekanizma: Wigner energy release overheating fuel, which ignited in the air-cooled graphite pile
ders: the UK moved to safer reactor designs and stronger regulation
yanilgi: The chimney filters were mocked as a waste of money. They trapped much of the radioactive material.
tartisma: Engineers pumped water into a burning reactor, not knowing if it would explode. Would you have?
basliklar: Why the Windscale Reactor Caught Fire
The Filter They Called a Folly
sahneler: A British nuclear reactor caught fire at Windscale.
For days the core burned, and radiation spread downwind.
Its graphite stored energy that had to be released by heating.
During that procedure, the fuel overheated.
Uranium and graphite began to burn.
Engineers finally flooded the pile with water.
Chimney filters, mocked as a folly, trapped much of the release.
Britain then moved to safer designs and stronger regulation.

baslik: A Candle Started a Fire Inside a Nuclear Plant
sonuc: had a cable fire that knocked out safety systems
tetik: a candle used to check for air leaks
mekanizma: candle flame igniting polyurethane foam sealant in a cable penetration
ders: US nuclear plants adopted strict fire protection and cable separation rules
zincir: CANDLE USED TO FIND AIR LEAKS
yanilgi: No reactor fault started it. A worker's candle ignited the foam sealing a cable passage.
tartisma: Using a candle to find leaks was common practice. How do risky habits become normal?
basliklar: The Candle That Set a Nuclear Plant on Fire
Why the Browns Ferry Fire Happened
soru: How do risky habits become normal?
sahneler: A fire broke out inside the Browns Ferry nuclear plant.
The fire spread for hours and knocked out key safety systems.
It was started by a candle.
A worker used it to check for air leaks.
The flame ignited foam sealing a cable passage.
Fire spread along the cables and cut power to controls.
Operators improvised to keep the reactors cooled.
US plants then adopted strict fire protection rules.

baslik: The Bomber Fire That Scattered Plutonium on Greenland's Ice
sonuc: crashed on sea ice carrying nuclear weapons
tetik: a cabin fire started by cushions near a heater vent
mekanizma: crash detonating the weapons' conventional explosives and dispersing plutonium
ders: airborne nuclear alert flights were ended
yanilgi: There was no nuclear explosion. The bombs' conventional explosives detonated and spread plutonium on the ice.
tartisma: Nuclear-armed bombers flew constant alert patrols. Was the risk worth the deterrence?
basliklar: Why the Thule B-52 Crashed
The Cabin Fire That Spread Plutonium
sahneler: A B-52 bomber carrying hydrogen bombs crashed onto Greenland's sea ice.
It exploded on impact, killing one crewman.
The fire started in the cabin.
Cushions had been stored near a heater vent.
The crew bailed out as smoke filled the plane.
On impact, the bombs' conventional explosives detonated.
Plutonium was scattered across the ice.
Airborne nuclear alert flights were ended soon after.

baslik: The Refinery Tower Overfilled for Hours Before It Exploded
sonuc: exploded during a unit startup
tetik: a distillation tower overfilled with flammable liquid
mekanizma: overflow through a blowdown stack venting to open air, igniting near occupied trailers
ders: trailers were moved away from process units and process safety oversight was strengthened
yanilgi: The explosion wasn't a sudden equipment rupture. The tower was overfilled for hours while instruments misled the operators.
tartisma: Staff trailers stood close to the unit to save walking time. How close is too close to a hazard?
basliklar: Why the Texas City Refinery Exploded
The Tower Overfilled for Hours
sahneler: A refinery unit in Texas City exploded during startup.
The blast destroyed nearby trailers, and fifteen workers were killed.
A distillation tower had been overfilling for hours.
Its level gauge gave misleading readings.
Liquid overflowed into a blowdown stack open to the air.
A vapour cloud formed and was ignited, probably by an idling truck.
The trailers were far too close to the unit.
Process safety oversight was strengthened afterward.

baslik: A Stuck Gauge and a Silent Alarm Caused a Giant Explosion
sonuc: exploded in a massive vapour cloud blast
tetik: a petrol tank overfilling while its gauge was stuck
mekanizma: overfill with a stuck level gauge and a disabled high-level switch, forming a vapour cloud
ders: fuel depots were required to install independent, tested overfill protection
yanilgi: The explosion was far more violent than anyone expected. Vapour cloud explosions at open sites were thought unlikely to be that powerful.
tartisma: The safety switch needed a padlock that was never fitted. How do small omissions disable safety systems?
basliklar: Why the Buncefield Depot Exploded
The Gauge That Stuck and the Switch That Didn't Work
sahneler: Early one Sunday, a fuel depot near London exploded.
The blast destroyed nearby buildings, and fires burned for days.
A storage tank was being filled with petrol.
Its level gauge had stuck.
A backup switch should have stopped the flow, but it wasn't working.
Petrol spilled from the tank and formed a vapour cloud.
When it ignited, the explosion was far stronger than expected.
Depots then had to fit independent, tested overfill protection.

baslik: Fertilizer Left in a Warehouse for Years Destroyed a Port
sonuc: was destroyed by a massive explosion
tetik: a fire in a warehouse storing ammonium nitrate
mekanizma: fire heating a large, long-stored stockpile of ammonium nitrate until it detonated
ders: ports worldwide reviewed hazardous material storage
yanilgi: The ammonium nitrate wasn't a new shipment. It had sat in the warehouse for years despite repeated warnings.
tartisma: Officials had written letters warning about the stockpile. Why did nobody move it?
basliklar: Why the Beirut Port Exploded
The Stockpile Left in a Warehouse for Years
sahneler: A massive explosion tore through the port of Beirut.
The blast devastated the city, and more than two hundred people were killed.
It began with a fire in a warehouse.
Inside were thousands of tonnes of ammonium nitrate.
The cargo had been seized and stored there for years.
Officials had sent warnings, but nobody moved it.
The fire heated the stockpile until it detonated.
Ports worldwide reviewed how they store hazardous materials.

baslik: Chemicals Stored Illegally Caused the Tianjin Explosions
sonuc: exploded in the port of Tianjin
tetik: nitrocellulose drying out and self-igniting in summer heat
mekanizma: self-ignition of dried nitrocellulose, then detonation of stored ammonium nitrate
ders: China tightened hazardous-chemical storage licensing
yanilgi: The warehouse sat much closer to homes than the rules allowed.
tartisma: Firefighters didn't know what was stored there. Should inventories of hazardous sites be public?
basliklar: Why the Tianjin Warehouse Exploded
The Chemical Store Too Close to the City
hook: They didn't know what was inside
sahneler: Two giant explosions ripped through the port of Tianjin.
Firefighters and residents were killed, one hundred seventy three in total.
It started with a fire at a chemical warehouse.
Nitrocellulose there had dried out in the summer heat.
It ignited on its own.
Firefighters didn't know what was stored inside.
The fire reached ammonium nitrate, which detonated.
China then tightened licensing for hazardous chemical storage.

baslik: The Small-Town Fertilizer Plant That Exploded
sonuc: exploded while firefighters fought a blaze
tetik: a fire reaching ammonium nitrate stored in a wooden building
mekanizma: fire in a combustible warehouse heating ammonium nitrate until it detonated
ders: ammonium nitrate storage and emergency responder guidance were revised
yanilgi: Firefighters weren't careless. Guidance at the time didn't make clear how close was too close.
tartisma: Homes and a school stood nearby. Who decides where hazardous plants can sit?
basliklar: Why the West Fertilizer Plant Exploded
The Fire Firefighters Didn't Know Could Detonate
sahneler: A fertilizer plant in the small Texas town of West exploded.
Firefighters were killed as they fought the blaze, fifteen people in all.
The plant stored ammonium nitrate in wooden bins.
It had no sprinklers.
A fire broke out in the warehouse.
The heat set off the fertilizer.
Homes and schools nearby were heavily damaged.
Storage and firefighting guidance were revised afterward.

baslik: They Used Dynamite to Loosen Fertilizer — It Exploded
sonuc: exploded, leaving a huge crater
tetik: dynamite used to break up caked fertilizer
mekanizma: detonation of an ammonium sulfate-nitrate mixture richer in nitrate than believed safe
ders: blasting of fertilizer stockpiles was stopped
yanilgi: Blasting had been done thousands of times without incident. A change in the mixture made it explosive.
tartisma: A method that worked thousands of times failed once. How do you notice when conditions quietly change?
basliklar: Why the Oppau Plant Exploded
The Fertilizer They Blasted With Dynamite
sahneler: A German chemical plant exploded, leaving a huge crater.
The town of Oppau was flattened, and hundreds were killed.
Workers had been breaking up caked fertilizer with dynamite.
They had done it thousands of times safely.
But the mixture had changed.
It contained more ammonium nitrate than before.
This time, the blast set off the whole pile.
Blasting fertilizer stockpiles was stopped after the disaster.

baslik: The Turbine That Blew Out of Its Housing
sonuc: flooded when a turbine was forced out of its housing
tetik: fatigued bolts on a vibrating turbine cover
mekanizma: fatigue failure of turbine cover studs under long-term vibration, letting water pressure eject the rotor
ders: Russian hydro plants reviewed turbine vibration limits and bolt inspections
yanilgi: The dam didn't fail. The water was released inside the power station when a turbine was pushed out of its seat.
tartisma: The turbine was kept running despite heavy vibration. How much vibration is too much?
basliklar: Why the Sayano-Shushenskaya Turbine Failed
The Vibration That Broke the Bolts
soru: How much vibration is too much?
sahneler: At Russia's largest hydro plant, a turbine burst out of its housing.
Water flooded the turbine hall, and seventy five people were killed.
The dam itself held.
The turbine had vibrated heavily for years.
The bolts holding its cover down were fatigued.
When they failed, water pressure pushed the turbine up and out.
Water poured into the hall.
Hydro plants reviewed vibration limits and bolt inspections.

baslik: Sugar Dust Blew Up a Refinery
sonuc: was torn apart by a dust explosion
tetik: sugar dust ignited inside an enclosed conveyor
mekanizma: primary dust explosion lifting accumulated sugar dust into secondary explosions
ders: combustible dust hazards gained attention from regulators
yanilgi: Sugar seems harmless. As fine dust in the air, it burns fast enough to explode.
tartisma: Dust had piled up across the plant. Is good housekeeping a safety system?
basliklar: Why the Imperial Sugar Refinery Exploded
How Sugar Dust Became an Explosive
sahneler: A sugar refinery in Georgia exploded and burned.
Fire swept through the buildings, and fourteen workers were killed.
The fuel was sugar.
Fine sugar dust had built up inside an enclosed conveyor.
When ignited, it exploded.
The blast shook loose dust piled around the plant.
That dust exploded in turn, spreading the damage.
Regulators gave combustible dust far more attention afterward.

baslik: A Spark, Methane and Coal Dust: The Upper Big Branch Explosion
sonuc: was ripped through by an explosion
tetik: a cutting machine sparking in methane
mekanizma: methane ignition that set off accumulated coal dust, with poor ventilation and worn cutter bits
ders: US mine safety enforcement and rock dusting rules were tightened
yanilgi: The methane flare alone might not have been deadly. Coal dust that should have been neutralized turned it into a massive explosion.
tartisma: The mine had many prior safety violations. When should a regulator close a mine?
basliklar: Why the Upper Big Branch Mine Exploded
The Coal Dust That Turned a Flare Into a Disaster
soru: When should a mine be closed?
sahneler: An explosion ripped through a West Virginia coal mine.
It swept through miles of tunnels, and twenty nine miners were killed.
A cutting machine sparked in pocket of methane.
The methane ignited.
Coal dust along the tunnels should have been covered with rock dust.
It wasn't, so the dust exploded too.
The mine had a long list of safety violations.
Mine safety enforcement was tightened afterward.

baslik: The Coal Waste Tip That Slid Onto a School
sonuc: slid onto a village school
tetik: heavy rain saturating a tip built over springs
mekanizma: liquefaction-like flow of saturated colliery waste on a slope above natural springs
ders: the UK passed laws to regulate the safety of mine and quarry tips
yanilgi: It wasn't simply rain. The tip was piled over natural springs, and earlier slips had shown it was unstable.
tartisma: Residents had warned about the tip years before. Why are local warnings so easy to dismiss?
basliklar: Why the Aberfan Disaster Happened
The Waste Tip Built Over Springs
sahneler: A mountain of coal waste slid down onto a Welsh village school.
It buried classrooms, and one hundred sixteen children were killed.
The tip had been piled on the hillside above the village.
It sat on top of natural springs.
Heavy rain saturated it until it flowed like liquid.
Residents had warned about the tip years earlier.
Smaller slips had shown it was unstable.
Britain then passed laws to regulate the safety of tips.
